discovery.notes: Direct WebFetch of guide.michelin.com returns HTTP 403 / AWS WAF JS challenge (x-amzn-waf-action: challenge), and no Chrome extension is connected, so pages were fetched via the r.jina.ai rendering proxy (prefix the URL with https://r.jina.ai/). CRITICAL URL gotcha: /th/en/... is only the LOCALE (Thailand-territory, English) and renders the generic worldwide list ("1-48 of 19,408 Restaurants", geo-sorted — I saw Vancouver restaurants); the correct Thailand REGION list is /en/th/restaurants. Option A (/restaurants/michelin-selected suffix) and option B (?distinction=michelin-selected) both still server-render the FULL unfiltered Thailand list ("Thailand : 1-48 of 485 restaurants") because the distinction filter is applied client-side by JS — so a Selected-only list does NOT come through; use full-selection instead. Verified working: page 1 = https://guide.michelin.com/en/th/restaurants shows "Thailand : 1-48 of 485 restaurants" with pagination to page 11; page 2 (/page/2) shows "49-96 of 485 restaurants". 485 = 10 pages x 48 + 5 on page 11. Cards expose distinction text per restaurant (e.g. "Bib Gourmand: Good quality, good value cooking"; stars likewise); cards with NO star/Bib label are the MICHELIN Selected tier. NOTE: live site now shows 485 total Thailand restaurants, not the 468 stated in the task (May 2026 additions), so the Selected count may now exceed 288 — reconcile after enumeration. Sample names seen verbatim: "Majchapasuk" (Udon Thani, p1), "Blackitch" (Chiang Mai, p2), "Sanae" (Chiang Mai, p2, Bib Gourmand).

spotcheck.notes: All 7 spot-checks passed. Evidence per item: 80/20 = live guide.michelin.com Bangkok page + listed in Michelin's own 'Full List of MICHELIN Star Restaurants Thailand 2026' article + third-party full list shows it under 1 STAR 2026. Euang Kam Sai = live Chiang Mai page, Bib Gourmand, one of 13 new 2026 Bibs. Baan Ta-Koh-Rai = live page (phra-nakhon-si-ayutthaya/restaurant/baan-ta-koh-rai), Bib Gourmand in 2026 guide — guide page title spells it 'Baan Ta Ko Rai' (slug baan-ta-koh-rai), same restaurant, spelling variant only. Jok Guay Jab Tom Sen Bat Queue (โจ๊ก ก๋วยจั๊บ ต้มเส้น บัตรคิว) = live Khon Kaen page, Bib Gourmand 2026. Aeeen = live chiang-mai-region page; absent from 2026 star list and all Chiang Mai Bib lists → Selected. Sartoria by Paulo Airaudo = live Bangkok page, added Oct 2025, NOT in full 2026 star list, no Bib → Selected. Indian by Nature = live chon-buri-region page, Michelin Plate/Selected mention in 2025 and 2026, explicitly not Bib. CAVEAT: guide.michelin.com blocks direct fetching (DataDome; WebFetch 403, curl 202-empty, Chrome extension not connected), so verification relied on site-restricted search snippets of the live guide pages plus Michelin's own 2026 star/Bib announcement articles, cross-checked against the Bangkok Foodies full-2026-list mirror. 'Selected' tier is never labeled in snippets, so it was confirmed by live-page presence plus verified absence from the 2026 star and Bib lists.

failures: Jaan (bib, Bangkok) — NAME MISMATCH: no restaurant named just "Jaan" exists in the MICHELIN Guide Thailand; the guide entry is "Jaan by Khun Jim" (guide.michelin.com/th/en/bangkok-region/bangkok/restaurant/jaan-by-khun-jim). Tier and location DO match under the full name: it is an official NEW 2026 Bib Gourmand in Bangkok & vicinity (Michelin's own 13-newcomer announcement, relayed verbatim by trueid.net and bangkokfoodies.com). If the dataset intends this restaurant, the stored name should be corrected to "Jaan by Khun Jim".
spotcheck.notes: Method: guide.michelin.com and viamichelin.com block non-browser fetches (AWS WAF 403/202 JS challenge) and the Chrome extension was not connected, so verification used (a) Wayback Machine snapshots of the actual guide.michelin.com pages taken AFTER the Nov 2025 Thailand-2026 announcement, reading each page's own data-dtm-distinction attribute and meta text, and (b) Michelin's official 2026 announcements relayed by third parties. Results: [1] Krua Khun Nid — snapshot 2026-02-07, distinction=bib, Udon Thani, meta \"Guide MICHELIN Thaïlande 2026\" → CONFIRMED bib. [2] เปลว (Plaew) — snapshot 2026-01-13, distinction=bib, meta \"2026 MICHELIN Guide Thailand\"; Michelin's site region label is \"Nakhon Pathom\" (nakhon-pathom-region URL), which falls under the guide's \"กรุงเทพฯ และปริมณฑล / Bangkok & surrounding\" press grouping → CONFIRMED bib (region acceptable, but note the site itself files it under Nakhon Pathom, not Bangkok). [3] น้ำย้อย (Naam Yoi) — snapshot 2026-02-13, distinction=bib, Phuket; also on phuket101.net's 2026 Phuket Bib list → CONFIRMED bib. [4] Rimsuan — Michelin spells it \"Rimsaun\" (likely their transliteration of ริมสวน); Feb-14-2026 snapshot of the official Ayutthaya listing shows Rimsaun with no bib/star marker, i.e., MICHELIN Selected (empty distinction = Selected on listing pages; bibs on same page show \"bib\") → CONFIRMED selected; minor spelling variance vs guide. [5] Scarlett — snapshot 2026-01-12, own-page distinction=plate (Michelin's internal value for Selected), Bangkok, \"2026 MICHELIN\" meta → CONFIRMED selected. [6] Loba Bang Niao — snapshot 2026-02-13, own-page distinction=plate, Phuket Region, meta \"a restaurant in the 2026 MICHELIN Guide Thailand\" → CONFIRMED selected (phuket101's 39-pick list omitted it, but the primary source page is unambiguous). [7] Jaan — reported as failure (name mismatch only; \"Jaan by Khun Jim\" is a genuine new 2026 Bib in Bangkok). Caveat: an on-announcement-day snapshot (2025-11-20) of Jaan by Khun Jim's page still showed distinction=plate — the site had not yet flipped to the 2026 bib status — but Michelin's official 2026 Bib newcomer list names it, so bib is correct for 2026.

sourceNotes.starsEN: Extracted exactly 43 restaurants: 2 three-star, 8 two-star, 33 one-star — matching the official Thailand 2026 counts. METHOD: The requested guide.michelin.com article returns HTTP 403 (AWS WAF JS challenge) under every locale slug tried (/th/en/, /en/) and via curl with browser UA, so it could not be fetched directly. Instead I used two corroborating fetched sources: (1) the official Michelin press release on michelin.com ("Thailand Shines Brighter with 10 New MICHELIN Star Restaurants"), which gives counts, statuses, the two 3-stars, both 2-star promotions (Anne-Sophie Pic at Le Normandie, INDDEE), all 3 one-star newcomers (Bo.lan, Cannubi by Umberto Bombana, etcha), all 4 promoted-from-Selected (Gaggan, Juksunchae, Nusara, Sushi Saito), and Green Stars; and (2) the Wikipedia featured list "List of Michelin-starred restaurants in Thailand" — I downloaded the raw wikitext and parsed the per-year star table programmatically myself (2026 column), yielding exactly 2/8/33. Every restaurant named by the official press release appears in the parsed Wikipedia list, so the two sources fully corroborate. STATUS values: NEW/PROMOTED per press release; RETAINED inferred from Wikipedia's 2025 column (same star count in 2025). NAME VARIANTS: Wikipedia writes "Inddee", "Le Normandie", "Goat" — I used the official press-release forms "INDDEE", "Anne-Sophie Pic at Le Normandie", "GOAT". GREEN STARS (5 total per press release): GOAT (new), Pru (PRU), Haoma, Baan Tepa — all starred and flagged greenStar:true — plus Jampa (Phuket), which holds a Green Star but NO Michelin star in 2026 and is therefore not in the 43. Locations are province-level from Wikipedia (39 Bangkok, 2 Nonthaburi, 1 Phang Nga, 1 Phuket); Thai-script names were not present in the sources fetched.
sourceNotes.starsTH: Source: Thai-language MICHELIN Guide article "รายชื่อร้านอาหารรางวัลดาวมิชลินประจำปี 2569 ทั้งหมด จากคู่มือ 'มิชลิน ไกด์' ฉบับประเทศไทย". Live guide.michelin.com returns HTTP 403 / AWS WAF JS challenge to both WebFetch and curl, so data was extracted from the Wayback Machine snapshot dated 2026-03-08 (second sourceUrl) of the exact same article URL. Counts match the article's own section headings: รางวัลหนึ่งดาวมิชลิน 33 ร้าน, รางวัลสองดาวมิชลิน 8 ร้าน, รางวัลสามดาวมิชลิน 2 ร้าน, รางวัลดาวมิชลินรักษ์โลก 5 ร้าน (Baan Tepa, GOAT [new], Haoma, Jampa, PRU). IMPORTANT on Thai names: the Thai article displays each restaurant name ONCE — Thai-named restaurants appear in Thai script only (nameThai copied verbatim; their roman 'name' is reconstructed from the restaurant URL slug present verbatim in the same source, e.g. slug "80-20" → "80/20", "bo-lan" → "Bo.Lan"), while international restaurants appear in roman only (no Thai script name shown, so nameThai omitted). Status "NEW" = ร้านใหม่ marker verbatim in the article. Two source-page bugs found in the raw HTML: (1) the Gaggan 1-star entry has a malformed link href="Gaggan" so no restaurant URL exists for it in this article; (2) the GOAT entry in the Green Star list mistakenly links to the baan-tepa URL — I used GOAT's correct URL from its 1-star entry instead. Cuisine types are not given in this article, so the cuisine field is omitted throughout. The article also notes Sühring is Thailand's second-ever 3-star and that 7 restaurants received a new 1 star (Bo.Lan, Cannubi by Umberto Bombana, etcha, Gaggan, Juksunchae, Nusara, Sushi Saito — matches the 7 NEW-marked 1-star entries).
sourceNotes.green: All 5 candidates CONFIRMED; none refuted. Official total = 5 Green Stars in MICHELIN Guide Thailand 2026 (michelin.com official article: GOAT 'joins the four establishments already recognized: PRU, Haoma, Jampa, and Baan Tepa'). GOAT is the only new Green Star this edition and is a One-MICHELIN-Star Contemporary Thai restaurant in Bangkok (per michelin.com). Tier caveats: the official Green Star announcement does not state tiers for the four existing holders, so tiers were sourced from secondary full-list coverage — Bangkok Foodies 2026 full list (PRU 1 star, HAOMA 1 star, Baan Tepa 2 stars, GOAT 1 star NEW; Jampa appears only in the Green Star section) and Phuket101 (PRU is Phuket's ONLY starred restaurant in 2026; Jampa explicitly 'doesn't hold a star' = Selected). Baan Tepa's 2-star status is corroborated by guide.michelin.com article titles ('a Two-MICHELIN-Star Restaurant in Bangkok'). Fetch limitations: guide.michelin.com pages (including the sustainable_gastronomy listing) and tatnews/chiangraitimes/thailand-business-news returned 403/bot-verification, and aroimakmak refused connection, so the official listing page itself could not be read directly; verification relied on the official michelin.com corporate article plus cross-checked secondary sources. Cuisines beyond GOAT's were not stated in fetched sources and are omitted rather than guessed.
sourceNotes.bibOfficial: COMPLETE: all 137/137 Bib Gourmand venues of the MICHELIN Guide Thailand 2026 extracted, 13 marked NEW. METHOD: (1) The official article guide.michelin.com/th/en/article/michelin-guide-ceremony/bib-gourmand-thailand-2026 is behind an AWS WAF JS challenge (403 to WebFetch, challenge page to curl), so I fetched its Wayback Machine snapshot — it names only the 13 newcomers plus per-province counts, not all 137. (2) For the full list I pulled Michelin's own public Algolia search index (app id 8NVHRD7ONV, public search key embedded in every guide.michelin.com page, found in the archived listing page; queried with Referer guide.michelin.com): index prod-restaurants-en filtered distinction.slug:bib-gourmand + country.slug:th returned exactly nbHits=137, every hit guide_year=2026 — the live 2026 selection. Names/cities/cuisines copied verbatim from that official data source. VERIFICATION: province counts match the official article exactly — Bangkok & Surrounding 44 (Bangkok 32, Nonthaburi 5, Nakhon Pathom 3, Pathum Thani 3, Samut Sakhon 1), Ayutthaya 8, Chiang Mai 18, Chon Buri 5, Isan 28 (Khon Kaen 11, Nakhon Ratchasima 8, Ubon Ratchathani 3, Udon Thani 6), Ko Samui 2, Surat Thani 7, Phang-Nga 6, Phuket 19 = 137; and all 13 newcomers from the article matched (4 BKK-area: Jaan by Khun Jim, Keawloon, Kolun.h, SANN; 1 Ayutthaya: Khanom Mho Kaeng Mae Yai (Phai Ling); 3 Chiang Mai: CHAWEE, Euang Kam Sai, Gongkham; 1 Korat: Nub; 1 Udon: Pad Thai Bua Dang; 2 Surat Thani: Dear Phangan, Nampetch; 1 Phang-Nga: Krachang Khao Lak). CAVEATS: the index lists the newcomer "Jaan by Khun Jim" under the short name "Jaan" (slug jaan-by-khun-jim — same restaurant, kept verbatim). NEW flags come from the official pre-announcement article (the index's own new_table flag has been reset to 0 for all, as expected mid-cycle). 4 venues are indexed under Thai-script names (บ้านสวนลุงไข่ Ko Samui; ครัวเก๋ากึ๊ก a.k.a. Krua Kao Kuk, ชวนชิม, หมอมูดง Phuket) — copied verbatim, also placed in nameThai. Ko Samui rows are city=Ko Samui, province=Surat Thani (the guide counts Ko Samui separately from Surat Thani). No Bib venue carries a Green Star (green_star null on all hits). Most url fields are empty because I only retained Michelin short_links where present in the payload; canonical URLs can be built as guide.michelin.com/th/en/{region-slug}/{city-slug}/restaurant/{slug} if needed. Chrome extension was not connected; archive.ph and web.archive.org are blocked for WebFetch (used curl for Wayback).
sourceNotes.bibMediaEN: FULL 137-NAME LIST CORROBORATED. Source of the complete enumeration: AroiMakMak "Michelin Guide Thailand 2026" (English-language Singapore-based Thailand food blog by Wilber Suen, published 2025-11-27), fetched via Wayback Machine snapshot 20260303112010 because the live site refused connections (ECONNREFUSED/timeout). Names copied verbatim from that source. Reconciliation: my per-province counts sum to exactly 137 with exactly 13 (NEW) flags, and match the officially announced distribution reported independently by Nation Thailand and Khaosod English (44 Bangkok+vicinity [32 BKK-group + 3 Nakhon Pathom + 5 Nonthaburi + 3 Pathum Thani + 1 Samut Sakhon], 8 Ayutthaya, 18 Chiang Mai, 5 Chon Buri, 28 Northeast [11 Khon Kaen, 8 Nakhon Ratchasima, 3 Ubon Ratchathani, 6 Udon Thani], 2 Koh Samui, 7 Surat Thani, 6 Phang-nga, 19 Phuket) and NEW breakdown (4 BKK+vicinity incl. SANN in Nonthaburi, 1 Ayutthaya, 3 Chiang Mai, 1 Nakhon Ratchasima, 1 Udon Thani, 2 Surat Thani, 1 Phang-nga). CAVEATS: (1) Mainstream English media (Nation Thailand, Khaosod English, Pattaya Mail, Friday Bangkok, thailand.go.th) enumerate ONLY the 13 newcomers, not the full 137 — AroiMakMak is the only accessible English source with the full enumeration, so treat it as a blog-tier corroboration. (2) Transliteration discrepancies between AroiMakMak and Nation Thailand for the newcomers: Jaan by Khun Jim vs "Jan by Khun Jim"; Keawloon vs "Kaew Loon"; Kolun.h vs "Ko Loon"; Khanon Mho Kaeng Mae Yai (Phai Ling) vs "Mae Yai Thai Custard (Phai Ling branch)"; CHAWEE vs "Chavee"; Euang Kam Sai vs "Ueang Kham Sai"; Gongkham vs "Kong Kham"; Nub vs "Nhab"; Pad Thai Bua Dang vs "Pad Thai Bua Daeng"; Krachang Kao Lak vs "Krachang Khao Lak"; Nampetch vs "Nam Phet"; and notably "Dear Phangan" (AroiMakMak) vs "Thung Phangan" (Nation Thailand) for the Surat Thani newcomer — this last one differs beyond spelling and should be reconciled against the Michelin primary source. (3) guide.michelin.com and khaosodenglish.com returned HTTP 403 to WebFetch; Khaosod was retrieved via curl and corroborates 7 newcomer names. Khaosod names verbatim: Jaan by Khun Jim, Keawloon (Bangkok), Khanom Mho Kaeng Mae Yai (Ayutthaya), CHAWEE, Gongkham (Chiang Mai), Nub (Nakhon Ratchasima), Krachang Khao Lak (Phang-nga).
sourceNotes.bibMediaTH: Full 137-restaurant Bib Gourmand 2569 (2026) Thailand list extracted VERBATIM from PPTV HD36 (pptvhd36.com/travel/food/261911). Verification: (1) downloaded raw HTML via curl and parsed the <h3>/<li> article structure programmatically with Python — all 137 names are physically present in the page source, not summarizer output; (2) per-province counts (กรุงเทพฯ และปริมณฑล 44, พระนครศรีอยุธยา 8, เชียงใหม่ 18, ชลบุรี 5, ขอนแก่น 11, นครราชสีมา 8, อุบลราชธานี 3, อุดรธานี 6, เกาะสมุย 2, สุราษฎร์ธานี 7, พังงา 6, ภูเก็ต 19 = 137) match the officially reported distribution repeated by Matichon, TrueID, Siamrath, Thainewsonline, Gourmet & Cuisine and Marketingoops; (3) the 13 NEW entries (status=NEW) match identically across all 7 sources. Caveats: the Thai sources give Thai script only — no roman/English forms were shown, so name = nameThai (Thai script verbatim; a few names contain Latin words as part of the actual name, e.g. ครัวแล้วแต่ R-ROM). Cuisine fields are filled only for NEW entries where the source described them; greenStar not covered by these articles. เกาะสมุย is listed as its own section in the source (administratively part of สุราษฎร์ธานี) — kept as-is. จันทร์หอม appears twice (Bangkok and Koh Samui) in the source — two distinct restaurants, both kept. The official guide.michelin.com/th/th article returned HTTP 403 and could not be used directly.
